titleStmt.title: A volume of rhapsodical meditations and visions (Rawl. D. 1262)
titleStmt.author: Ann Bathurst

editionStmt.p: Digital edition led by Naomi Baker. First pass transcription by Finch Collins.

div1.p:
The God of Abraham, the Fear of Isaac, & The Authors Inducements the Strength of Israël; even The God & Father of our Lord & Saviour Jesus Christ taught me whilst I was yet young: He taught me to goe, leading me by the armes Hos. 11. 3. in footsteps that I knew not, yet understood I not that it was He yt led me; but afterwards when more of age I perceived He taught me step by step, how I should walk in a Child-like Obedience to His Divine Attributes, with large Leadings in His Mercifull Love- Nature-Love, giving me great experiences of His Mercifull Love, and greatly to acquiesce in all his wise Dispensations; thus teaching me that His wisom knew what was best, and that His Fatherly Love was so great as all should work together for good to Them that love Him, and are called thereunto. And though His teachings & Conduct I for many years concealed, and so intended still; yet since recollecting what use it might be off for my self and others, I was much press'd -- in Spirit toto write Them down, as also afterwards solicited by some ffriends so to doe, for the better reception of what further Manifestations The Lord now in these later dayes has made declared unto me (not for my self only but others also.) Therefor I'm not willing to hide it in a napkin, well knowing that the same spirit wch led me is but one Spirit, and will teach all that do but adhere thereunto; for God is the same yesterday, to day & for ever: who at sundry times Heb. 1. 1, 2. and in divers manners spake in time past unto the Fathers by the Prophets, hath now in these last days spoke to us by His Son, whom He hath made Heir of all things; putting all things under Him, spoiling all Principalities & Powers. For in that He put all Heb. 2, 8. in Subjection under Him, He left nothing that is not put under Him: but now we see not yet all things put under Him; but we see Jesus crowned with Glory & honour, yt at the Name of Jesus the Saviour, that saveth his People from their Sins, every knee should bend, all Homage, glory & honour, & Obedience Phil. 2. 10,11. of Things in Heaven, & things in Earth, & things under ye Earth should be given: and yt every Tongue should confess that Jesus is Lord to ye glory of God the Father, to whom be glo-
ry & honour, dominion & praise now, henceforth & eternally.

I was taught as I've said when I was young. The boughs when young & tender will yeild easily, so it is with ye tender soul before it grows old in sin. And surely as the first fruits & firstlings of the fflock God required should be offer'd & sacrificed to Him, so is the first of our age: wch, as it is the most acceptable to God, so it is the most easy to Man; not having then such loads of guilt, if The Accuser should attempt to awaken.

It is I say much easier, yet not altogether easy: for about the Tenth year of my age, I found the Accuser awaken in me a sence of sin, yet not of any one particular Sin, for I could remember none, but as if all my life had been a continued act of Sin: wch caused in me such great horrour & anguish, of as even to despair of mercy; or at least to question whither I could expect mercy: but I was soon stayed with David's praising God in the 30th psalm (hearing a sermon ps. 30. 1,2,3. on it) I will extoll Thee O Lord! for Thou hast lifted me up and hast not made my foes to rejoyce over me: &c. So yt my sorrow ecchoed my joy. And in another sermon I learned watchfullness at all tymes, lest Sathan should gett advantage over me, even to watch the use of things lawfull, & against all or any appearance of evil. All which I still acknowledge I owe first to God, & secondarily much was suck'd in from pious Parents & Religious education, whereby both by precept & example I was accustomed to pray.

And about the fifteenth year of my age for my encouragement to pray thereunto, I obtain'd a promise in Prayer, yt the same should be answered; declaring to me how, & by what sign I should know yt That prayer was answered. Wch was decordingly fulfilled at its appointed season. And having had such experience how God heard, & in hearing answered, it did for the future encourage me in all the pressures of my soul, to pour out my requests unto Him, who has required ps. 50. 15. yt we should Call upon Him in the day of trouble, and hath also promised He will deliver us; and then we must glorifie Him. and we do best glorifie Him by believing unto Obedience.

About the Eighteenth year of my age; seeing the strict practice of some about me, it awakened in me a serious search how it was with my soul, to what end I was born, and to what end I ought to live? and finding Little to accuse my self off, as to sins of Commission, I enquired into sins of Ommission; Dan. 6. 10,13. and in Scripture record I found yt Daniel prayed three ps. 119. 164. times a day, and David said, seven times a day do I praise
Thee: (wch certain number may signifie many times, yet do I think yt David prayed seven sett times a day: for so He seems to insinuate, when he says, a.Evening, & morning, & at noon will a. ps. 55. 17.I pray. b.I prevent the night watches. c.at midnight I will arise b. ps. 119. 148. to give thanks unto Thee. I prevents the dawning of ye mor-c. v. 62.-ning & cried. &c.) and in 1. Thess. 5. 16. It is said; Rejoyce ever more, pray without ceasing, &c. but I thought it only referred to sett times; wch accordingly with all privacy I began: but my mouth was stopt like one struck dumb; wch caused great consternation & terrour, saying within my self; have I so many sins, and can I beg pardon for none? and so many graces do I stand in need off, and is there not any one Grace I can ask for? yet still did I remain as one stupified and dumb, but filled with an awakened horrour & grief even to high despair: wch soon was still'd with this Inward reflection, I was Nothing, & could do nothing, not think in my heart ofof God without Divine assistance: and His assistance makes our acceptance.

Several disturbing Objections arose, but still I was answered to study duly rather than reward; teaching me yt thô I could not read his secret-will, yet I could read his revealed will, wch requires yt I should serve Him (at this time I had taken in The doctrine of Election, of wch I was afterward undeceived.) 2. K. 7. 4.: and so in his strength I resolved to throw my self upon Him, in the simple sincere, Child-like Obedience, that if I perished it should be in so doing: wch reminded me of the Men that went into the Camp of the Assyrians, who said, if we sitt at the gate see nothing but death attend us; and if the Assyrians save us alive we shall live; and if They kill us we shall but die. This then was my case, and these words instructed me; and good was That God like an anchor of hope to help & draw me thus to Him! I continued praying, hearing & reading; but often was the return of sorrows lest I should labour in vain: and little was applied to me from a Sermon or reading but reproof through the awakned sense of sin; as if it were spoken to none but me, putting far off all comfort.

And in some few moneths I was seized with sickness, and that somewhat dangerous; as for my own part, being before a stranger to sickness I did not question but I should die; wch caused me to mourn & weep to them that were with me telling them, I had no assurance of a better Life, now that I fear'd I was to die, having lived a long time in sin (being now about eighteen years & an half old.) Then some of them said to me, yt I had been well educated & brought up in all sobriety; not knowing, nor having so much as heard of the vanities that most then walked in. I answered, 'tis true I had
been well instructed, & did practise what I was capable off: when I was a Child I loved to pray with my sister, & to hear her pray. I lik'd to read The Bible & good books, as for other books I thought them not worth my time & pains since wch time I've hardly read any thing save the Bible and I further said, yt I knew not of any one sin I lived in, wch was some stay, but it soon went off: and I said, all this is nothing; I did but like a Child little understanding what I did. [sideways dagger pointing right] A few days afterwards, all my sins were laid before me (as they were also some years agoe, as I have already said.) yet not one particular sin remembred, but yt all my whole life was like one act of sin, and that Hell was to receive me: I said I had deserved the hottest place of it: and I saw Hell open to me, a great black, dark pit; and I at the brink ready to go in: I acknowledg'd to the Lord He was very just if He did cast me in; and also yt He was very mercifull in keeping me out so long in the Land of the Living. I concluded & said yt now Hell was my portion, and God was to be praised for his long forbearance to the Children of Men; for He had been a just God if He had cast me into Hell and soon as I was born, for I had been conceived in sin & brought forth in inquity.

And as the Lord taught me He was just & mercifull, so He made me to consider his power, whither He was not able to save me out of this horrible Pit, thô I had deserved it. I did verily believe God was able to save me, though I was at the very brink of Hell just a going in; but whither God was willing to save me, this I feared; and thus continued a day or two: Then it was answered, if He was not as willing as well as able, none could have been saved; for it is only of ffree Grace yt we are saved, and how dost thou know but yt God will save thee? I said, what, me? Yes, thee. I said, I have nothing yt is good in me, a poor sinfull Creature: what is there in me yt God should pardon me? Then I was answered, 'Tis true nothing is in Thee, but (The Lord spake wth power) I will have mercy because I will have mercy, & because mercy pleaseth me; and I have pardoned thy sins freely, and will remember them no more. Most gladly did I receive this word, It putt more joy & gladness in my heart, than They have when ps. 4. 7. [sideways dagger pointing right]their corn & oyl & wine encreased. [sideways dagger pointing right] And as before I saw Hell open'd for me, so now I saw the Heavens open and an Angel in the Heavens ready to receive me. I had some questioning of this, how I could expect such mercy as this, being not worthy; I was answered, if God stayed to shew mercy till we were worthy to receive, we should never have mercy. Some other Objections arose to the like purpose, but all were answered; and so answered as never to question his Love, nor could The Tempter ever sett footing to disturb my peace & comfort ever since: but once
when Sin wrestled in me (as Esau & Jacob) I look up Rebekkahs speech & said, if it be so, why am I thus? if the Lord hath pardon'd me & graciously accepted me, why then doth sin still strive to overcome me? to make me speak unadviseably thô not sinfully? Then I lookt back & call'd to mind, how God came in by a mighty hand & a strong arm, and pulled me out of the claws of Sathan, & brought me from the Gates of Hell. And then considering how the Lord spake peace & silenced all my doubtings, and how He freely accepted me, and also the raptures of joy I then had; these & such like remembred made my spirit say, it is so, thôugh I am thus. Then how willing was I, yea I even longed to be with Christ, wch is best of all: to see That Christ wch I had now but a taste off, to see Him face to face; but had some desire after this, to live to glorify God; yt I might shew forth His praise that had done so much for me; but The Lord told me, He was all-Glorious in himself & needed not any Creature to sett forth his Glory. Then I thought what was I? God had many in the world He could make use off to sett forth his Glory, to declare it to the world, though I weremight be call'd out of it. And I said, The Lord hath carried me on from strength to strength, and as He hath begun a good work, and hath gone on, so He will perfect it to the day of Redemption: He is the same yesterday, to day, & the same for ever.

I further said, now Lord, what wait I for! my expectation is from Thee; my soul longeth for Three, for the Living God; when shall I come & appear before God? O the dread of wicked men! They call for mountains to fall on them, and the Hills to cover them, but O the sight of God is the Heaven of Heavens! ThoseWe that wait for & expect such things as these, what manner of men & women ought we to be in all holy conversation & godliness? How exact in our words, laying a watch on our lips & putting a bridle to our tongues, yt we sin not wth our mouths? How should we, as Christ did, go about doing good; and when God hath converted us,--strenthen our Brethren? We should communicate of our experience to others, we should not want grace by this, but we should encrease our graces: we should be in no Company without leaving some savour of good there, striving to season it. Oh the sins of Omission! how hard is it not to be guilty of omitting duties, that are required of every Man in their several stations & Conditions? besides the duties we omitt between God & the Soul, whereas it is our duty to pray; nay it is our priviledge & happiness yt God will hear & accept our prayers, yt He should let us converse & meditate on Him, and permitt us to fetch a Turn in Heaven, and that every day, yt we may be in Heaven by Meditation, as it were before our time, and receive the first ffruits of our spiritual Canaan in this Life. In keeping God's
Commandments ther's great reward even in this Life, as well as Eternal Happiness & enjoyment of God for ever hereafter: nay the Comfort a Child of God enjoys in this Life in God will make ammends for any afflictions He undergoes for God besides. yt He will also give them Eternal mercies for every where there shall be no end, but They shall praise God to the longest line of Eternity: O the hight of this Mercy! O the length, the breadth & deepth of Love! Who is able to comprehend it! to know the Love of Christ that passeth knowledge.

Thus for ten years & more, I was led as in a Land of Love, being much accompanied with joy & peace; and often in Meditation, as I was carried forth to various sibjects, sometimes of the Love of God, sometimes of the vanity of the Creature: other times I meditated of the unsuitableness of all things in this world wch can nowise be satisfying to an Heavenly desyring soul: But my most usual meditations & admirations were of the Love, mercy & pity of God to false Man; so yt I was as one that could see nothing but Love, and in all could desire nothing but to be swallowed up in Him, & to be taken to Him; wch earnest desyre was hard to be subdued, and to be contented to [sideways dagger pointing right] wait my appointed time till my change come. [sideways dagger pointing right] Many great & eminent answers of Prayer were given, scarce anything I ever askt in prayer, but was answered: he never gave me a desire to ask, but He allwise had a Hand to give and I did often know when I should not ask, by being straitned & could not, so yt by freedom to prayer, or restraint not to pray I knew his will: and though I found it my duty to ask, yet offer'd up my desire allwise to his will, not daring to have any will, whither for my self or others. As for the Things of the world, I willingly did not take thought for to morrow. Of This much might be written, but I forbear.

At the end of these Ten or eleven years (wch was about the 30th year of my age) having some Difficulties to pass through I still bore up: but sometime after the sorrow prevailed: and not having skill to stand fast in the Christian armour, I was as one taken out of a Land of *Apr. 3rd 1667. peace: I felt it as the same hour, even to a minute,* how I was taken out of the Peace & Rest, and immediatly putt into a wilderness to be tempted: where I was to fight my way through, & with the Three great Enemies of Man, viz. the world, the flesh, & the Devil. And as soon as by ffaith & prayer one seem'd to be weakned, a second did rise up; and as soon as that temptation seem'd to be overcome, a third arose up: so yt I had no time to go off my watch, and even fainted thrô long waiting. And when I did think, & sometimes hope they were dead, then an unexpected one would awaken
so yt at length when I found a sweet Calm, I knew by experience, it was a Cordial before some storm or Trial in the wilderness, where the world, the flesh, & the Devil maintained a continual war, yet did I never question my former comforts, neither was I all this time without great Teaching, & joy in God; in visions of the night when asleep, and some few in the day; wch allwise taught & declared what I was to pass through.

Thus was I carried on about Ten years more; and near the end of these years I felt some great Thing was to be knowen & enjoyed, but knew not what: and I had an hungring desire to know further of God, and how I might understand aright how to worship Him as He required; and yt I might rightly apprehend the Intercession of Christ for us; how He was our Advocate with the Father, and how I should direct prayer to God through Christ; wch I searched in the Scriptures, but could not understand it as I beleived it might be knowen: I was extreme sensible of my own Ignorance, how little I knew of God, and how ignorant of my self, even as one knowing nothing. And as I had near ten years desyred a redeption from my former state, for though I was much stayed & comforted yet I found there was a greater Interruption in my thoughts than I had had formerly; so I did greatly press for the days of old, saying; O that it were as in the days of old, when the candle of the Lord did shine round about me; when I sat under his shadow with great delight! O when wilt Thou restore unto me the joys and stilness of thy Love!

After this for my support, on June 23d/ 1678, a year of Jubilee was proclaimed, & prophesied to me by an Angel or Spirit in a Dream or vision; and after confirmed by another Angel in such a lyke dream, which was as They had said, and at the same time performed to me, to witt, at the end of six moneths, being December 23d/ 1678. But about a moneth or three weeks before, I was brought to that, as to be fully contented to take up my Cross dayly, if it was His will; being satisfied to wait the Good-pleasures of God not desireing deliverance as I often before had done. And I was no sooner contented (as I have allwise found yt contented Resignation is the nearest way to deliverance) but in three or four weeks at most, on Decer 23d/ aforementioned, I was taken out of this Bewildred place, and put into such a calm as is not to be expressed: that as the very day, hour & minute of my being set in the wilderness were so plainly felt & perceived, being so different an air; so the taking out of it was as sensible, leaving all storms behind me I was as fel into a sweet still
Heaven, and new senses given me as one not in a Body; so yt I felt my self quite taken out of all disturbances of outward sense and sett in a new air or another climate, and another spirit given me that was accompanied with new understanding; being as one who had putt off an old garment, nay like one uncloathed of this mortal Body, and a new Body brought forth to manifestation; wch caused great joy & admiration much more felt than can be expressed.

And in a few moneths after, there opened a view of the Heavenly Canaan (as followeth) ffor wch and for the many Manifestations of The Eternal Love of The Father, through His Son of Mercifull Love, communicated By his Holy and Blessed Spirit, I offer to God alone all the praise, honour, Glory, power & dominion of things in Heaven, & things on Earth, & things under the Earth, as is most due: To whom be Eternal Praise. Amen!

div1.head: A Transportation or Manifestation made to Me, whither in the Body or out of the Body (as Paul saith) I cannot tell; but I was often made sensible; where my Body lay, and that my Eyes did abide open, by my spirit's return to it. which was on Mundays night March 17th 1679.
div1.p: Being in Contemplation of Mount Zion, and earnestly longing to be in Mount Zion state, and also to understand what that extreme Agony meant, wch I had been in fourteen days before, that held me about half an hour when I was in bed. It was like a Dark fflood cast forth from the Dragon, wch was ready to swallow me up; but my alone Defence was Prayer, crying without ceasing, & saying nothing else for the greatness of my Anguish & fear, but O Jesus! O Jesus, hide me in thy wounds! Thus for the space of half an hour, till there became a most blessed & gracious Calm!

And being very sensible of the difficulty of overcoming The Beast & Great Dragon, and to gett out of the Babylonish Principle in our progress towards Heaven, my longing grew still stronger to be in Mount-Zion. And as I was in these desires I thought, but what if God should come & appear to me at this instant? upon wch The fflesh seem'd to retreat, & recall her earnest suit, as framing to my self that the sight of God was terrible. But Faith soon check'd those fleshly ffears, by representing yt This was the Place, wch I did groan, thirst & long for; and yt till I was fitted & made meet for this Inheritance of The Saints in Light, I earnestly desired some comfortable Prospects & Visions of that Glory, as Others have had, to encourage me during my wandrings in this Howling Wilderness; This I say, I had often press'd after, manely, to have some Tastes of the Heavenly, till I should arrive at the fruition of it, thereby to stay my holy impatience: yet at the same time I was afraid lest the sight of such a Glory should make it more difficult for me, to be content to stay here in the Body; and should encrease my thirst, even to fainting for The Living God. These thoughts made me pour our my request crying out, O stay me with flagons, & comfort me wth Apples, for I am sick with Love! [sideways dagger facing right] And soon after, it being then near [sideways dagger facing right]half an hour past eleven at night, as I lay looking up by the Spiritual Eye of ffaith, I saw Paradise with the Tree of Life
in the midst of it, very pleasant & not to be compared to any thing here below: the ffruits that grew upon it were of the most beautifull & plesant Colours; the leaves were of a most fresh & lively green; the grass under it was young & tender, & of a pleasant green Tincture; I could see no weeds, and all appeared as it had been newly watered.

Yet did not This fully satisfie me; except I might also see the Kingdom of Christ; Then was I caught up higher, where I saw Jesus in the appearance of a Man, all surrounded wth a most glorious Light, wch greatly transported me; for now I knew I was come to the place wch I had so long desired to behold. Whilst I was here I appeared to my self (I mean my Angel appear'd to me, but I understood it not) at wch being surprized, and the fflesh shrinking at the greatness of the Glory, I perfectly felt a Touch on the top of my head, wch drew my spirit out of me, as you would draw a knife or sword out of a sheath, & it cut as it was drawn forth, I felt it cut like a two-edged sword. Thereafter I appeared as a spark of Light, and according to my desire I sometimes mounted up to see Jesus; and then descended again to Paradise; all wch motions were very swift.

After this I desired to see the Father, and after a little stay in the Kingdom of Christ, I was had up to God the Father. But Oh! Oh! Oh the Glory! the Splendor! the Brightness! the exceeding unexpressible Glory that was there! at the sight of wch I threw my self down before Him, crying continually for above a quarter of an hour; My God! My God! I'm now come to the place to wch Thou hast called me; and wch I so long desired to see. I am now come ot enjoy Thee! Thee! being got above all those difficulties I have been so long wadeing through, to witt; The Kingdom of the Great Dragon & Beast with its Babylonish Principle. I can't express the delight I look to see my self redeem'd from all those burthens, letts & hinderances I had so long groaned under. [sideways dagger pointing right] Then I saw the Dragon was of a long shape & of a green colour like a serpent; It had four short legs, the foremost the longest; It was terrible to behold, the very thoughts of it since made me almost to tremble: It appeared as if it had lost its prey and given it over. The Beast appeared like a grey-Lyon, & seem'd very eager & fierce to find what was become of his prey; but I feared him not, being extremely pleased to see my self so safe. But soon after the Beast saw me & fixed his great Eyes upon me,
wth his jaws wide open, as one watching for the Prey, wch was in the sight thô not out of his reach. The Bablyonish Principle lay on the ground in the appearance of toys and triffles of several sorts, & of puppets for Children. They were represented to me as if they had been spued out, and therefore were not to be taken up again.

I desyred also to see Hell, wch I saw at a distance, in ye likeness of a dark smoaking ffurnace; even a thick darkness wch comprehended no light. [sideways dagger facing right] Then My God told me (as I sat [sideways dagger facing right] in a Cloud of light & in the felt Embraces of God the Father his Divine Love, wch I thought I was to abide in for ever, never to go out) that I was not come up to abide there as yet, but yt I was first to pass the briers & thorny way; Paradise being hedged about wth thorns; and none can enter into it but by passing thrô the Thorns & Stones. Then I lookt down [manicule] to Paradise and saw such a thorny & stonoey way as I had never seen before; being all stones, and no path-way to be seen, nor any Body walking there; the stones were half as high as my self: sometimes it appeared all stones, sometimes all Thorns, and those the highest that ever I had seen to pass. I endeavoured to go, but could not tell where to tread; I took care yt no long Garment might hinder me. I thought I would enquire of Travelers that went that way to direct me (though I saw none) but presently I was check'd wth [looped ribbon] The more we advance in our way to Heaven, thô the difficulties become greater, yet through Grace & Experience we are strengthned to go faster. a stay; They need a Guide themselves. I ecchoed back again, Lord send thy Spirit Truth to guide me! I look'd very earnestly to see whither I could see any one in the same way wth me; at length I saw one whom I knew, who came forward thô the way was very bad, & up hill; and I saw yt the higher she came the faster she went; thô the way seemed worse & worse[looped ribbon].[dagger facing right] But at last the Thorny way seem'd to Hide [dagger facing right]away & disappear, and in stead thereoff appeared a pleasant River of Glass, wch compassed Paradise; and Paradise appeared much more beautifull & pleasant than before.

Then I desired to behold Christ again, and to see his Heart, as some had seen, wch I beheld flameing wth Love to the saints. Then I desired to enter into the Heart of Christ, and so I did; entring & coming forth again very swiftly
for several times. After this, I was desirous to enter into whole Christ; and presently I was in the Person of Christ, where I felt & saw my self: I saw my Eye in & through Christ's Eye; and I saw my head, neck & breast in Christ's, as through a Glass; so I was satisfied. Yet I desired also to see & feel, whither my hand was in Christ's hand, and I found it was; and I laid hold on the hand of Christ with my fingers, and it felt to the hand that touched, as if it touched another hand; but to the hand that was touched, as if the right hand took hold of the left; (upon which my Spirit returned to my body, and I was much amazed; for I did not think yt I belonged to my body, or should ever have returned to it again: but soon was I caught out of my body again, more swift than an arrow out of a bow:) yea I saw my whole Man in & thrô the Transparent Body of Christ; wch sight did cause unexpressible joy in me, to see yt Christ was One wth me, and I one in Him; The blessed Union, wch I had long desired clearly to understand.

After I desired to see God the Father sitting on his Throne of Glory wth a Rainbow over his head: This was an unexpressible great Glory & Majesty, streaming forth Beams like a Glorious Sun; thô infinitly transcending That we see here in our Orb: in wch Glory were most beautifull & Lustrous colours, somewhat resembling the Colours & compass of a Rainbow, but far more beautifull; wch I beheld [dagger facing right] wth great admiration.[dagger facing right] I desired likewise to see Christ in his vesture dipt in Blood: then was I immediatly transported into his Glory, and saw his Majesty cloathed wth a Loose Garment; the outside of wch was of the colour of pure Blood; but the Inside was as Lined wth white; wch while seem'd to spread it self over most of the red. I was taken up sometimes wth the admireing Consideration of Christ's Love, whilst I saw his Love-flameing Heart, from wch some Blood streamed forth, and also several silver Chrystaline streams. Thereafter I saw the Son of God in his vesture of Glory appear at the Right hand of the Father, who appeared as before, on His Throne surrounded wth an unexpressible Brightness & Glory, and The Rainbow encompassing all.

I desired also to see the Holy Spirit, wch I saw in the appearance of pure silver Chrystaline streams on the left hand of the Father. Then again I saw the Three, Father, Son & Spirit united into one great Glory, making one great Glorious Light: and I went into Them wth The Elders, and we were all one great Light: Then again They appeared Three
as before; and the Elders apart, and I apart: and I beheld Their Glory. And again I was swallowed up, like a smaller Light of a greater; and changed into the same Glory several times. But none can expect expressions from me answerable to those wonders & Glory, wch there I beheld; they being indeed beyond all expression.

Still continuing to behold this Glory I saw no Angels, and therfore desired to see Them; and immediatly there were several of them compassing part of the Throne: They were like unto transparent Gold, wth faces like Men, having two large golden wings coming forth of each five of their faces, wch was most glorious. [dagger facing right] After this, seeing The Streams come [dagger facing right] forth from the Heart of Christ, as I had seen before, like to a Transparent silver, I asked, what it was? He said, it was the ffire wch was to purifie the saints. Then I had a mind to see the wounds of Christ, and I looked on his Hands, and the wounds there did glister like the purest part of the Light, wch I saw in God the Father, comparing them together. Thus I abode in this Glory, and would often go into the purest part of the Light of God the Father, and be one wth the ffather; and then come out again, & return as often as I would.

I desired to have an Ancient Christian of my acquaintance there, (who I knew had for a long time desired to see this Glory) that He might come & enter into this Light, from whence God is called the Father of Lights; and a little after He came. Then I desired yt one of my Children might come up, & she came a little after: and then anotehr of them; and so till all were come in: They came in the same order as I had desired it. ffirst of all my ffriend entred into the Pure Light; then all my Children, one after another: and as they came up, I remembred Two little Children, wch died one at fourteen weeks, the other at fourteen dats end; and imediatly as soon as I began to desire it, They came like two Bright Sparks, one after another, and entred into this great Light and became one with it; as a Spark is swallowed up of the flame; then They came forth again, to witt, my ffriend & Children, wch were then living, in the same order as They went in; they first wch went in first; all severally, yet all as one case of bodies, I seeing Them all/together, and yet severally through each other.

Then I desired to see all the saints come up to this Glory, and saw Them come like a Glorious White Cloud, two & two together, thick & close, a little behind the right hand of Christ: They penetrated ^ through his heart, came forth again, and entred into ^ into Christ's Body, and the midst of the Glory of the ffather, as we had done before: and
so there passed an innumerable Company, and they still ascended without ceasing, till I ceased to behold, and then They came out of the Father again in the same order as They entred in; they first wch went in first; all severally, yet coming all out thrô each other; wch was wonderfull. All of them sat down round the Throne, wch was then of a very vast largeness; The Elders & Saints sitting roung it: I looked to see whither the Saints had Corowns like the Elders, and I saw They had; though I saw they had none, till They had gone thrô Christ into the Father, and were come forth again, and satt down about the Throne. Their Crowns, as I thought were all of a size, they sitting in great order: the Bottom of the Throne was like one smooth glass. There were many more Angels than I had seen before, all like the former compassing the Throne; on the backside, as 'twere of the Saints & Elders, a little above their Crowns; where They might be fully seen.

Reb. 5. 6. Then I thought what the Lamb was, wch S. John speaks of, saying, there stood a Lamb as -- It had been slain: and I looked, and by the midst of the Throne, near the left side, at the foot of the Father there stood a Lamb, wth its right side towards me, having a bloody place in its neck; and some blood was upon the wool as if blood had run down from the wound: It was alive. Then I desired to hear the Saints sing, All honour & praise to Him that sitts on the Throne. Hallelu-jah! But fearing lest I should not be able to behold so glorious a Melody, I fainted, yet hearkned, and when I could not hear Them sing, my Spirit sand praises to Him that sat on the Throne; but I cannot remember what I sung. I still beheld ye Glory untill it began to descend nearer, and the nearer It came, the less was the Light & Splendour: I said, The Glory is the less the nearer the Earth it comes, or is it not because my Eye of ffaith is somewhat dimmed? Then pressed I with a streaching forward, that ffaith might not fail, but yt I [dagger facing right] might see the Glory as bright as I had seen it: [dagger facing right] Then the Throne disappeared and was gone; and I saw the Glory of the Father of Lights, far exceeding any I had seen before like to transparent Gold mingled wth a ffirey Light, wch shined down to the Kingdom of the Son. This Glorious Light shined in great beauty thrô the Kingdom of the Son into Paradise below it, as a Reflexion of the first pure Light, and it became more beautifull by far than before shading an unexpressible beauty over all the Trees and flowers, wch appeared all transparent. After this, there was a Sheet of Light drawn before
this surpassing Glorious & beautifull Light; and another Little Sheet seem'd to descent from it like a Cloud of Light upon the Thorny ground, and lay upon it; I saw it as long as I lookt after it, it being near two in the morning when this cast appeared; the whole having lasted about two hours. But the Idea (or representation) of all remained fresh with me, from ye first to the last of it, for some days together yr after.
One thing is observable, yt nothing of all I desired was denied me, but the hearing of the Saints sing, wch I desired wth some fear, otherwise than I had done all the rest.

There was towards the end of This vision as I came nearer the Earth, a Request put up by me (finding I had nothing denied me) Lord, what wilt Thou doe wth This Nation? and Straight way there appeared an Hand & arm stretched out towards Them, with a slight moving of the Hand twice, looking like the waving or putting by of my Request, wth these words; Concern not your self with That: Implying yt I was to attend to my Inward Teachings, and not to look out after National Concerns, or the publick affairs of the world: it being said, saluteing nothing by the way. But Oh! The ravishing & unexpressible joys I felt, when I sat in the delightfull Embraces of the Divine Love! a joy, which as it could never be apprehended by me before, so neither can it in the least be express'd by me now. And 'tis very observable, when God told me I must go down again, because I was not as yet come up there to abide; and when I saw the Beast & Dragon ready to receive me, I was not in the least displeased, neither found I any desire to the contrary, nor any fear; but found my self wrapt up in a quiet stilness, acquiescing in the will of God; with a great Delight in the present Enjoyment, finding my self above the reach of evils for the present.
Severall things are here set down short of what they might have been expressed; but all infinitly beyond any thing that ^ was can be anywise declared of them.

div1.head: June 11.
div1.p: Soon after I was a bed being perfectly The vision of a Beautifull Rock by a Still River. Wth a Glorious Sun ariseing on it. awaked, I saw by the Spiritual Eye, a very pleasant still River, and a Bridge went cross it, riseing in the middle like ane Arch, but narrow; I went to goe upon stone steps (which were there) to goe on the Bridge to a Rock I saw on the other side; but when I came near to climbe, The Bridge went higher like a Cloud or Rainbow; so that I saw, it could not be walked on by a weighty body of flesh, but ane Aërial Body; for the Bridge was a Cloud of air: then I contented my self to look on the further side of the River to the Rock, and I saw most pleasant Greens, wch grew as 'twere out of the Rock; The Rock was exceeding high & large, it appeared like several Greens, and after of other pleasant colours, extream pleasant & beautifull in great variety & beauty: it seemed still like a Rock but a Roack of wonder, the more I wondred at the beauty, abundantly more beautifull it appeared; yet no great Light, but shaded. [dagger facing right] On [dagger facing right]the right side of This Rock ^ began to arise, but it was so exceed- ^ a Glorious Sun -ing glorious that I trembled, and could not behold it, then it went down; after, it arose a little again, but I could not bear it, so it disappeared, though I had a desyre to have born it, and looked for it; and if I did but look towards it, it began to appear; as if it did declare that nothing hindred its ariseing, but my weakness yt could not bear it; and thereby shews his tenderness to compassionate our weakness being in bodys of thick clay.

div1.head: June 12th.
div1.p: Being desireous to have this pleasant object continued, and further to understand this Rock of wonder, the Idea of rock remained; I saw growing forth of this Rock innumerable fruitfull Trees, cloathed as 'twere wth very large leaves, & large pleasant fruit like Citrons, but mixed with red; the beauty being very pleasant & lovely; as also ^ how it was placed ^ considering by so pure, still & shady a River, and how various This Rock had presented it self the night before, still desired to see fully it being as 'twere in a shady place; not to be perfectly perceived. After, this vast high Rock had other Trees thick & close of small leaves, and so curious, as if it had been pure Gum-work overspreading it from the top to the bottom, like the side of ane High Hill or Mountain. After there appeared like Clouds a Sea wth waves; then a Still River: [cross symbol] [cross symbol] Cloud again like a Hilly Country wth a Brook running betwixt two hills, where I saw ye first pure River: and by this Brook appeared a Rock but not so pleasant as That before.

div1.head: June 18 & 19th.
div1.p: I saw many small flowers, some white & some blue, and of other pleasant colours grew up on the Rock, as I looked on them, Many fflowers grow out of the Rock in great variety. and gone again, and immediatly others in their room, scarcely to be discerned what flowers they were, by comeing up so quick; and as one disappeared, other came; & so continually '' in great variety.of ffl; and a swift passing away of the Hills & Heavens, but the Rock stood still.

It appears transparent, wth flowers of red & white only; and why? The next day, there was a thick Body of Darkness or Plate of black before a Bright Light, wch shined under the darkness and lighted the Rock; do the Rock looked transparent with flowers of red & white, no other colour; I asked, why red & white only, and no other colour amongst so many flowers? It was answered, to shew the Purity of the Saints when washed in the blood of the Lamb.

div1.head: June 21. 22.
div1.p: Its Brightness makes all round it appear like a beautifull Landship. The thick Body of darkness, (wch the day before had still remained before the Light) came over me, and I was gott beyond the darkness, between the darkness & the Light, which I had much desired; and there was so pure a skie of all colours, as if the Rock had stread its transparent beauty over the Heavens & Earth; so that there appeared a most beautifull Landship every where, and as in a Glove. Then appeared the Rock, having full sight of it, by reason ^ be towards of a pure light, but yet the back seemed to ^ me: I said, why must I be at the back of it, and not come before to see the Treasuries Its Treasures of Pearle. of Pearle? then it turned to me, where there was such measure of pearle as cannot be expressed, over the whole side of the Rock, going out of it. And I saw my self (my Spirit or Angel) goe Her Angel appears like one pure Pearle. from me, as a pure body of Oriental Pearle, like all one pure Oriental pearle, it seemed such a shineing Beauty; but ye ^ (my Angel) back of it^ was only towards me. The Idea of this Beauty doth ^ me, greatly rejoyce^, that our vile Bodies shall be made like his Glorious Body.

It is adorned wth flowers of Pearle & Rich Stones. Next day I saw the Rock so gloriously adorned wth goodly Pearls & precious Stones, as it was wonderfull to behold; so that I might glutt my sight with seeing: yet after that appeared some thing most rare for curiosity; it was fflowers of pearle, & Rich stones, wch grew in the shape of flowers, with the leaves of pearle in curious shapes.

div1.head: June 23.
div1.p:
As I lay awake (for so all hath appeared, although the ^ or Representations of the whole Idea^ remaines the day after) . This Rock still appeared in its full lustre & great riches, being loaded with many larger Rich Stones, and the Light appeared very splendid before it in flameing streames, wch greatly delighted me. This Light continued, but the Rock disappeared for some tyme; and there Ane Altar with a fflameing Heart. appeared Ane Altar with a flaming Heart upon it, till it became a large fflame as big as the Altar: and at some distance from the Ane Arbour of transparent Flowers. Altar, appeared a most Beautifull Arbour of all pleasant flowers, transparent & of a great length, scarce to be seen at the farthest end; the Bottom as of glass; I looked into it and went in, seeing through the fflowers the Light that lighted it, not as between; but as thrô variety of coloured pure Glass of Transparent flowers: I would have been made Transparent & Swallowed up in them, the beauty was so great; as I have done some other times, when greatly delighted with the Rock, I would have been taken into it, and would sometimes goe & sitt in the hollow of the Rock, under -- Its shadow to content me, seeing I could not be taken into it. The Altar I saw flame several tymes as often as I lookt towards it.
Then I looked for the Rock, and it appeared again: and the Arbour appeared various in its fflowers to what it had before, being larger & fewer greens, more whitish with great beauty: and the skies appeared like a beautifull Landship. I was held in this about an hour at least. The first sight of the Rock was in a shady place, but it ascended still higher & higher, so as Beauty did more fully appear, far above any before.

div1.head: June 25.
div1.p: The Rock is taken into The Pure Light & becomes one with It. After appears as one Oriental Pearle. Still desyreing further to behold the gloruous wonder of the Rock for if we shall seek, we shall find; it appeared with greater glory all over Pearle, and a pure pleasant Light lighted it, & came over the Rock and took it into the Light; so the Rock was become one with the light; then the Light gave back to one side, to shew me that the Rock was in the light; and the Rock appeared like ane Oriental Pearle; and then I understood the Light and the Rock was all one Glory, even the God of Glory. O great was the delight to have such a clear sight of that Rock, wch is Light & Love! O the beauty of holiness! I would have been taken in to it. What shall I say of it? it is beyond expression, no tongue can utter it;[as S. Paul said, He heard things not fit to be uttered, So]This glorious Glory, we have not tongues fitted to express: I'm lost to go about to declare or sett it forth: if you understand what glory is, then you may give a guess to this ravishing overpowering splendidness; I here cease, and express it best, by saying nothing more than Glory! Glory! ^ silently transported ^ being with the rays of its beauty.

It appears as several Pearles united into one, to shew the Unity of the Saints in God. After, The Rock seemed to be several Pearls united unto the one Rock, all as of one Pearle. Then I asked, how This Rock of glory being before but one pure Pearle, appeared like many united into one? It was told me, The Lord was that great Pearle of price, that as his Pearles were many, and yet united into one great Pearle, it shewed ^ the Unity of the Saints, when they come to that ^ such is great pearle of price, and awere made one wth Him; They're made one, by being united in the Rock, like^ growing out of the one Pearle, ^ the Seveal pearles severally every one founded, & made one with the Rock, though severall pearles.

The reason of the Rocks appearing so variously at first. Then I asked, why the Rock had appeared so various before it came to that Beauty of Glory, it seeming to be as a gross thick Body at first appearance thô beautified upon it? It was said, it is to declare the drossiness that which is in the Saints, and how They grow into this Glory by degrees; and when come to this fullness of Glory, all dross iwas done away, They awere so clarified that they become a like transparent with the Rock. [dagger facing right] The purifying Light must enter the soul ere it can enter into the Light. Then I desyred to enter into this Glorious Light, it being like a glory of Light, but I was told; This Light must first enter into me, to purifie and burn up all the dross, yt I may be purified to enter into this pure Light; then I desyred with panting and hungred & thirsted, reaching forth my whole affections wth strong desyres; and as I panted, it came with ^^ a great overshadowing, penetrating, nay filling; and as I breathed forth my [looped ribbon] This was a feeding on Christ's flesh, & a drinking of his Blood. earnest suit, it still breathed in sweet fresh gales of the Spirit, penetrating me throughout.[looped ribbon] Then I desyred The Saints might feel the same I did, and breathing out desires, I felt as if virtue went out to a ffriend (then sick and brought to my Spirit^) and I emptied, but hasted to the ffountain, where was enough to fill me and others; for I had
only what I had received, and wanted it breathed forth to others; but this can be as little expressed, as before I said of the Rock: but it was a sweet Life, Love, power & virtue overpowering and filling me with joy, delight & praise; and such one intimate ffamiliarity as if I might have, & do what I pleased, conversing with God as with ones intimate ffriend; nay more, as with ones self.
